title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: Datadog
providers.scope_notes: IP documentation differs on entitlement (Pro+ via support vs Enterprise). Confirm contract. AWS WIF requires supported integration/configuration.

controls.name: Workload Identity Federation identity and intake mappings
controls.what: Only AWS role ARNs matched by a mapping can authenticate, and each identity mapping grants exactly one Datadog user or service account's permissions.
controls.setting: Organization Settings > Workload Identity Federation > Identity Mappings / Intake Mappings; cloud_auth API
controls.plan: Not stated on page; requires Datadog-AWS integration
controls.quote: Each mapping grants a cloud role the permissions of a specific Datadog user or service account.

controls.name: Workload Identity Federation Write permission
controls.what: Only roles with this permission can add, change or remove federation mappings (Admin role by default).
controls.quote: Add, update, and remove workload identity federation configurations

controls_unknown: No org setting found that blocks personal application keys or forces service-account-only keys.

Whether the IP allowlist applies to API-key and client-token requests outside telemetry intake is not stated; entitlement differs between account docs (Pro+/Enterprise) and API reference (Enterprise).
Plan requirement for Agent-based WIF: current WIF page lists no tier; earlier material says Enterprise-only and preview.
How to delete or disable an identity mapping is not documented on the WIF page; intake mappings are deleted via API.
Whether custom roles (needed to narrow these permissions) require a specific plan was not confirmed.

authentication.summary: Organization API key, often combined with a user/service-account application key; OAuth for supported apps; workload federation for supported scenarios.

federation.details: AWS identity (assumed-role ARN) maps to a Datadog user/service account for a temporary JWT (Terraform) or to an intake mapping for a managed API key (Agent). AWS is the only supported cloud; Agent flow not on US1-FED/US2-FED sites.

ip_restriction.boundary: Org IP allowlist applies to UI/API, with documented intake/public-dashboard exceptions. Not a per-key rule.

lifetime.summary: Short-lived JWT; Datadog returns an expiry with the token; official Go client assumes 15 minutes if none is returned

renewal.summary: Terraform provider re-signs an AWS STS request to get a new temporary JWT. Agent receives a Datadog-managed API key that Datadog rotates; on failure the Agent falls back to the API key in datadog.yaml.

administration.summary: Application-key scopes, service accounts, role permissions, OAuth grants, IP allowlist and key revocation.
administration.conditions: IP documentation differs on entitlement (Pro+ via support vs Enterprise). Confirm contract. AWS WIF requires supported integration/configuration.

inventory.details: Identity mappings can be listed (Organization Settings > Workload Identity Federation, or GET /api/v2/cloud_auth/aws/persona_mapping); issued JWTs are not listed.

expiry.api: Read the expires attribute in the POST /api/v2/delegated-token response; not configurable (Go client assumes 15 min if absent)

token_format.notes: Terraform flow gets a temporary JWT; Agent flow gets a Datadog-managed API key. No documented format.

log_sources.name: Datadog Audit Trail
log_sources.notes: Request events for API calls plus product events; records @auth_method and key IDs. Default 90-day retention when enabled (3-90 days); 7 days when disabled.

log_sources.name: AWS CloudTrail (customer side)
log_sources.notes: Role sessions whose credentials sign the STS GetCallerIdentity request.

containment.steps: Delete intake mapping (DELETE /api/v2/cloud_auth/aws/intake_mapping/<MAPPING_UUID>); remove persona mapping; disable mapped service account; revoke the AWS role session on the AWS side.
containment.notes: JWT lifetime not documented; Agent may fall back to configured static API key.

credential id field for federated sessions

calls.reveals: Log events, as the mapped user or service account
calls.log_notes: WIF JWT is used for later API calls as the mapped identity; logs query appears as Audit Trail 'Query (Public Beta)' event.
